# SA lines only: render with digital-demand-factory/screen-demos/generate_two_voice.py

[intro]
SA: "Configuration can only choose between adapters that already exist. Moving from key-value items in DynamoDB to relational rows in PostgreSQL needs new code. This clip shows how much, and where it lives."

[screen_01]
SA: "This dated capture shows the prepared before state: PostgreSQL has been removed from the adapter registry. The later capture restores the adapter and runs its contract tests. The video replays those results without changing the checkout."

[screen_02]
SA: "The completed replay added one PostgreSQL adapter file and one registry line. This dated capture shows the adapter path, the unchanged domain and application, a clean architecture check, and the completed contract test. The video reads the capture; it does not apply a patch."
SA: "The shared contract ran against memory, DynamoDB, and PostgreSQL. A real database move would still need data conversion and cutover."

[screen_03]
SA: "Read the contract, not the insertion count. Create uses an upsert, so PostgreSQL keeps the port's overwrite behavior. The schema has no foreign key from orders to users, because the other adapters accept an order for an unknown user. Whether that rule should change is a product decision, not something one adapter should decide quietly."
SA: "The contract tests check create, read, list, delete, overwrite and missing records the same way on every store. If PostgreSQL answered differently, we would have changed business behavior while calling it portability."

[outro]
SA: "This does not migrate data, and it is not free. It is about two hundred and twenty lines of adapter code plus tests, and a real move still needs data conversion and a cutover. What the architecture gives you is a contained blast radius: the work lives in one adapter, and one contract tells you whether behavior survived."
SA: "The takeaway: configuration changes the store, an adapter changes the technology, and the core stays put."
